Diagnostic accuracy with independent reader reproducibility

ClinicoPath

Source: vignettes/oncopath-reader-reproducibility.Rmd
oncopath-reader-reproducibility.Rmd

Plan the independent readings

Specify the scoring scale, clinical cutoff and direction before looking at results. Readers should score independently, using the same instructions and appropriate blinding. Retain original readings before discussion or adjudication. Record how the reference diagnosis was established; a consensus made from the same readings is not an independent reference. Software can analyse the readings but cannot establish that they were independent.

Stoieva and Fraga’s systematic review found that 73 of 84 dermatopathology IHC studies reported no interobserver agreement measure. Their proposed combined score could be calculated in only three studies. See the PubMed abstract. The workflow below reports accuracy and reproducibility separately, with an optional experimental composite. It does not claim to reproduce the full-text review methods.

Use one row per specimen, one column per reader, and optional reference, specimen ID and patient ID columns. Patient IDs identify repeated specimens, not different readers. The supplied example has 180 fictional specimens, 90 fictional patients and three readers.

library(ClinicoPath)
data("ihc_reader_reproducibility", package = "ClinicoPath")
head(ihc_reader_reproducibility[c("case_id", "patient_id", "reference", "score1", "score2", "score3")])
#>          case_id     patient_id reference score1 score2 score3
#> 1 Fictional-C001 Fictional-P001    Absent     24     11     19
#> 2 Fictional-C002 Fictional-P001    Absent     11     24     44
#> 3 Fictional-C003 Fictional-P002   Present     60     74     87
#> 4 Fictional-C004 Fictional-P002   Present     79     64     91
#> 5 Fictional-C005 Fictional-P003    Absent      5     40     35
#> 6 Fictional-C006 Fictional-P003    Absent     38     26     37

Numeric cutoff: accuracy and disagreements together

In Pathology Interrater Reliability, select Numeric clinical cutoff as the reader workflow and expand Reader Accuracy and Cutoff Agreement. Select score1, score2, score3 as numeric readers, reference as the reference and the two ID columns. Enter Present and Absent as the reference positive and negative labels. Use the illustrative cutoff 50, the >= rule and near-cutoff width 5. Neither cutoff nor band is an IHC recommendation.

result <- pathagreement(
  data = ihc_reader_reproducibility,
  readerWorkflow = "numeric_cutoff", readerScores = c("score1", "score2", "score3"),
  caseID = "case_id", readerCluster = "patient_id",
  referenceStandard = "reference", referencePositive = "Present", referenceNegative = "Absent",
  clinicalCutoff = "50", positiveRule = "ge", nearCutoffWidth = "5",
  readerPopulation = "both", readerCaseLimit = 12,
  readerBootstrap = TRUE, bootstrapSamples = 1000, seed = 42,
  readerConfidence = .95, readerCode = TRUE)
result$readerDataSummary$asDF

Sensitivity is TP/(TP+FN); specificity is TN/(TN+FP). Balanced accuracy (BA) is their arithmetic mean. Each reader’s available-case accuracy uses that reader and the reference. The shared-case accuracy view uses only rows complete for all selected readers and reference. These are distinct populations; inspect both denominators before comparing readers. Missing or indeterminate calls are never counted as negative.

Each pair uses its own available readings, even if no cases are complete across all readers. Near-cutoff cases are those where either member of that pair has a score within the inclusive band, here [45,55]. They form a conditional subgroup, not a new accuracy cohort. Both directional discordance counts are shown. A disagreement alone does not identify which reader is wrong. The case-list limit affects display only; all eligible cases contribute to the estimates. Original dataset row numbers disambiguate repeated specimen labels. Tables support jamovi’s usual copying and export.

Binary calls and original ordinal agreement

For already classified calls, choose the binary workflow and enter exact reader labels. Extra labels are counted as indeterminate. The example’s call1 to call3 include explicit indeterminate calls in addition to missing readings.

binary <- pathagreement(ihc_reader_reproducibility,
  vars = c("call1", "call2", "call3"), readerWorkflow = "binary",
  readerPositive = "Positive", readerNegative = "Negative",
  referenceStandard = "reference", referencePositive = "Present", referenceNegative = "Absent",
  caseID = "case_id", readerCluster = "patient_id")
binary$readerDataSummary$asDF
#>        reader total missing indeterminate usable
#> "1"     call1   180       5             2    173
#> "2"     call2   180       5             2    173
#> "3"     call3   180       5             2    173
#> "4" Reference   180       0             0    180

Ordinal cutoff mode requires ordered factors with identical declared level order. In jamovi, set each grade’s measure type to ordinal and its level order to Absent < Weak < Moderate < Strong. CSV files do not preserve this metadata; the R dataset does. Select Moderate as the positive boundary and >= as the rule. Specify near-boundary categories as exact labels separated by semicolons in the interface (for example, Weak; Moderate). R callers can also use newline-separated labels as below. Ordinal categories are not treated as numeric distances.

ordinal <- pathagreement(ihc_reader_reproducibility,
  vars = c("grade1", "grade2", "grade3"), readerWorkflow = "ordinal_cutoff",
  ordinalCutoff = "Moderate", positiveRule = "ge", nearCutoffLevels = "Weak\nModerate",
  wght = "equal", referenceAccuracy = FALSE)
ordinal$readerOriginalAgreement$asDF
#>                 pair   n weight     kappa
#> "1" grade1 vs grade2 168  equal 0.5605929
#> "2" grade1 vs grade3 168  equal 0.4611749
#> "3" grade2 vs grade3 168  equal 0.5034695

The original-score table reports the chosen weighted kappa; the cutoff table reports unweighted binary kappa. Neither substitutes for the other. Choosing Standard agreement restores the existing categorical workflow, whose reference sensitivity and specificity are explicitly macro-averaged across categories.

Uncertainty and its limits

For independent cases, sensitivity, specificity, observed agreement and discordance have exact binomial intervals. BA, kappa and specific agreement use optional percentile bootstrap intervals. With a patient ID, all intervals require whole-patient resampling: every specimen from a sampled patient is retained, including repeated draws of that patient. Point estimates remain specimen-weighted. Readers are treated as fixed; these intervals do not support inference to a population of readers.

Bootstrap intervals are exploratory. A reproducible audit with 300 simulated studies per scenario and 399 draws found conditional 95% interval coverage of 92.7–94.0% for 240 independent cases with unequal margins. With 60 clusters of three perfectly correlated specimens, coverage ranged from 91.3–93.0%; BA coverage was 91.3% (Monte Carlo 95% interval 87.6–94.3%). Thus the method does not guarantee nominal coverage. With eight clusters or rare categories, intervals were frequently unavailable. See tools/validate_reader_intervals.R and the CSV audit under literature/reader-reproducibility-validation/ for all results and Monte Carlo intervals.

Any undefined draw, undefined point estimate or constant bootstrap distribution suppresses the affected interval. Counts and reasons remain visible. Negative finite kappa is retained in agreement inference. A minimum of two sampling units permits computation, but does not establish adequate precision or coverage. More resamples reduce simulation noise; they do not fix sparse-data or small-cluster coverage.

The separate agreement analysis now offers this exploratory method for specific agreement. Its existing approximate Wilson method remains the default because the coverage audit did not justify replacing it with a purportedly validated method. Both methods state their limitations. Its specific-agreement table retains complete cases across all selected raters, which differs from pathagreement’s pairwise masks.

Optional experimental combined score

Select one reader pair and explicitly name which member supplies BA. The module-specific score is sqrt(BA * kappa), computed on cases complete for that pair and the reference. It is unavailable for negative or undefined kappa; a valid zero is retained.

exploratory <- pathagreement(ihc_reader_reproducibility,
  readerWorkflow = "numeric_cutoff", readerScores = c("score1", "score2"),
  clinicalCutoff = "50", referenceStandard = "reference",
  referencePositive = "Present", referenceNegative = "Absent",
  readerCluster = "patient_id", readerPairs = "selected", readerPair1 = "score1",
  readerPair2 = "score2", showKappaBalanced = TRUE, compositeReader = "score1")
exploratory$kappaBalancedTable$asDF
#>     reader             pair   n sensitivity specificity        ba     kappa
#> "1" score1 score1 vs score2 168   0.7349398   0.9411765 0.8380581 0.6989247
#>      estimate lower upper attempted valid undefined boundary constant
#> "1" 0.7653362    NA    NA         0     0         0        0    FALSE
#>                                  status
#> "1" Cluster intervals require bootstrap

This is an explicitly labelled extension, not a verified reproduction of the paper’s reader aggregation rule or a reporting standard. No clinical acceptance bands or automatic ranking are provided. Report the components as well as the combined value.

Plan sample size and record the analysis

Use kappaSizeCI() for precision, kappaSizePower() for a hypothesis test, and kappaSizeFixedN() for power with an already fixed subject count. These existing calculators require category proportions, a specified kappa design and 2–6 raters who each rate every independent subject. They do not directly size a study with repeated specimens, selected near-cutoff subgroups, missing reads or a random-reader estimand. See their help pages for the supported category counts and assumptions.

Record the independent-reading procedure, reference source, declared scale, cutoff and inequality, selected readers, class labels, missingness policy, case population, sampling unit, confidence method, seed and draw count. The Reader workflow settings table and optional R-code output preserve the analysis choices. Long resampling loops use jamovi checkpoints; select one pair when investigating expensive intervals.
